newsitem.title: USA: 96/97 Producer coffee ending stocks low - USDA.
newsitem.headline: 96/97 Producer coffee ending stocks low - USDA.

text.p: Coffee ending stocks in producing countries at the close of 1996/97 were forecast on Friday at 28.75 million bags, the lowest level since 1979/80, the Agriculture Department said.

World coffee exports in 1996/97 were forecast at 79.6 million bags, up more than 5 million bags from estimated 1995/96 exports. If realized, USDA said exports at this level will allow some rebuilding of depleted stocks in importing countries.

Coffee stocks in producing countries fell 7.9 million bags in 1995/96 and are forecast to drop another 3 million bags in 1996/97. A large drawdown in Brazil's stocks accounted for most of the change, but stocks also were cut in Central America and in African countries, USDA said.

World coffee consumption in 1995/96 was about 99.7 million bags -- 75.5 million bags in importing countries and 24.2 million bags in exporting countries. Use in producing countries in 1996/97 is forecast up 3 percent with most of the increase occurring in Brazil.

USDA said world coffee production for 1996/97 is forecast at 100.9 million bags, up 12 percent from last year and an increase of almost 2 percent from June. USDA first released this estimate on December 13.

Total coffee supply in producing countries in 1996/97 is forecast at 133.3 million bags, up 3.0 million bags from the preliminary 1995/96 level. All of this increase is coming from the higher level of production, as beginning stocks in producing countries are estimated to have droppped to 31.7 million bags at the start of the 1996/97 marketing year, compared with 39.6 million bags a year earlier.
Total exports from producing countries are forecast at 79.6 million bags, up 5.2 million bags from the previous year's level.
Brazilian coffee production was estimated at 27.0 million bags. The USDA first released this estimate Dec 13.

Coffee production in the Brazilian state of Mina Gerais was put at 14.0 million bags, down from 15.0 million last year. Production in the central/west areas of that state went down this year. Production in Espirito Santo was put at 5.4 million bags, in Sao Paulo at 3.4 million bags, in Parana at 1.2 million bags, and in other states at 3.0 million bags.
